name: FFIEC BSA / AML Examination Manual — operational examination yardstick
supervisor: FFIEC (FRB + FDIC + NCUA + OCC + CFPB + state liaison)

articles.title: Risk assessment — examiner expectation
articles.requirement: Examiner first reviews the FI's BSA/AML risk assessment. The expectation: (a) documented + comprehensive; (b) covers customer, geographic, product/service + transaction risk factors; (c) refreshed at least annually + on material change; (d) integrates the 8 AML/CFT National Priorities; (e) drives risk-tiering of customers + calibration of monitoring + EDD triggers. Inadequate risk assessment is the single most-cited Pillar 1 finding.

articles.title: Pillar 1 examination — policies + procedures + internal controls
articles.requirement: Examiner reviews: written program documentation; senior-management or board approval evidence + dates; risk-based design proportionate to size/complexity; coverage of all key BSA obligations (CIP, CDD, SAR, CTR, sanctions, EDD, recordkeeping); periodic review; updates to reflect regulatory change. Common findings: generic/template program not tailored to risk profile; weak controls in particular product lines (correspondent, private banking, digital assets); missing or stale BSA risk assessment.

articles.title: Pillar 2 examination — BSA Compliance Officer
articles.requirement: Examiner verifies: BSAO named + qualified; sufficient authority + autonomy + access to senior management/board; sufficient resources (staff + technology + budget); demonstrable ability to enforce compliance across business lines. Examiners test by interviewing the BSAO + tracing their decision authority + reviewing escalations. Common finding: BSAO understaffed relative to FI size or complexity; BSAO reports too far below CEO/COO to be heard.

articles.title: Pillar 3 examination — training
articles.requirement: Examiner reviews: training programme content + frequency + completion records; role-targeted delivery; refresher cycle (at least annual for AML staff); inclusion of current ML/TF/PF typologies + 8 National Priorities + sanctions evolutions + product changes; effectiveness assessment. Common finding: training generic + not role-targeted; senior management + board training thin; new-hire onboarding training delayed.

articles.title: Pillar 4 examination — independent testing
articles.requirement: Examiner reviews: most recent independent audit report; auditor qualifications + independence from AML function; frequency (annual is de facto standard for larger FIs); scope coverage (risk assessment + program effectiveness + transaction-monitoring + alert disposition + SAR/CTR quality + sanctions + training + BSAO authority); findings tracked to remediation through to closure. Common finding: audit scope too narrow; remediation tracking weak; auditor independence concerns.

articles.title: Pillar 5 examination — CDD + Beneficial Ownership
articles.section: FFIEC Manual — Customer Due Diligence + Beneficial Ownership
articles.requirement: Examiner reviews: CDD methodology for understanding nature + purpose of customer relationships; BO collection at account-opening (Beneficial Ownership Form or equivalent); 25% + control prong identification; ongoing monitoring + risk-based update of customer information; integration with CIP. Common finding: BO information stale + not refreshed; customer risk profile not updated on material change; CDD documentation inconsistent across business lines.

articles.title: SAR filing — quality + timeliness examination
articles.requirement: Examiner tests: SAR filing timeliness (30/60-day windows); narrative quality (the 5W's — who, what, where, when, why — plus how); supporting documentation retention; non-filing decision documentation; SAR escalation + governance. Examiners pull a sample of SARs filed + a sample of cases not escalated to SAR + reverse-engineer the FI's judgement. Common finding: late SARs; poor narratives; thin or missing investigation files; no documented basis for no-file decisions.

articles.title: CTR filing + structuring detection examination
articles.requirement: Examiner tests: CTR filing accuracy + timeliness (15-day); aggregation rule application (same-day, same customer); CTR exemption Phase I + II maintenance; structured-transaction detection (the 'structuring scenarios' — multiple sub-threshold transactions designed to evade reporting); SAR filing for detected structuring. Common finding: missed aggregations; weak structuring-detection scenarios in transaction monitoring.

articles.title: EDD examination — correspondent + private banking + high-risk customers
articles.section: FFIEC Manual — Correspondent / Private Banking / High-Risk Customers
articles.requirement: Examiner reviews: identification of high-risk customers + accounts (correspondent / PEPs / SFPFs / cash-intensive businesses / MSBs as customers / nested correspondent / virtual-asset exposure); EDD methodology proportionate to risk (source of wealth + source of funds + enhanced ongoing monitoring + senior-management approval); periodic refresh. Common finding: PEP identification incomplete (especially domestic PEPs + family members); SFPF accounts without adequate SoW/SoF; correspondent EDD documentation thin.

articles.title: Special topics — digital assets + RIAs + cyber
articles.requirement: Recent FFIEC + agency updates incorporate: (a) digital-asset exposure (CVCs in customer-onboarding + transaction monitoring + sanctions screening; blockchain-analytics integration); (b) Registered Investment Advisers (in BSA scope from 1 January 2026 per FinCEN final rule); (c) cyber-incident SARs + ransomware-specific procedures (post-OFAC ransomware advisories); (d) trade-based money-laundering (TBML) typology integration; (e) elder-fraud-specific procedures (per FinCEN 2022 advisory).
